Source: Reuters

Posted February 23, 2000
February 22, 2000
Canada hemp growers await payment from U.S. firm

See
DEAland Attack On Canadian Hemp Industry
Draws Sympathetic Coverage In Agricultural Press
and
Canadians Find That Hemp Fields Are No Rose Garden.
Starting A New Crop Has Many Complications

WINNIPEG, Feb 22 (Reuters)
(MarijuanaNews note: It is interesting that Reuters would pick up the story at this early stage. It is very unusual for something like this to be reported before any default.)

- Canadian hemp growers who grew seed for the new industry last year are now trying to collect on late payments from U.S. firm Consolidated Growers and Processors Inc. (OTC BB:CGPR.OB), an industry official said on Tuesday.
See
Consolidated Growers And Processors Delivers 100 Tons Of Hemp Seed To Manitoba
Via World’s Largest Cargo Plane

" They're two-and-a-half weeks behind on their payment. They've paid a third to some of the growers,'' said Joe Fedowich, chair of the Parkland Industrial Hemp Growers.

The telephone went unanswered at the Winnipeg office of CGP, which last year said it would build two hemp processing plants in the province of Manitoba after the Canadian government legalized the growing of hemp in 1998.


See
Depressed Commodity Prices Cause Explosion In Western Canadian Hemp Planting
– Too Much Too Soon?

Calls by Reuters were not returned from CGP's California office.

Fedowich said 220 hemp growers in the Prairie provinces of Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Manitoba were owed C$1.5 million, due at the end of last month.
(MarijuanaNews note: The Canadian dollar is around 70 DEAland cents.)

" Some growers received none of the money, some received a third of the money,'' said Fedowich, who said he was also unable to reach company officials.

Most of the hemp growers are located in Manitoba.
See
Sending The Right Message:
$6 Million Hemp Processing Plant In Rural Manitoba " Sends a very strong signal to farmers. "
and
 " Manitoba used to be one of the major growers of industrial hemp before it was banned 1930s. "
It May Be Again.

The growing of industrial hemp has been viewed as controversial because it is grown from the same cannabis sativa plant that produces marijuana. Industrial hemp contains much less of the drug than its illegal brother.

Legalization of industrial hemp in Canada has provided an advantage to Canadian growers over their counterparts in the United States, where such crops are largely illegal.

Nine U.S. states last year passed legislation allowing research, study or production of hemp.

" We've all got a three-year contract signed with CGP,'' he said, adding that farmers still had the seed in their possession and did not wish to sell it until they had a clear message from the company.

Industry estimates said Canadian growers were expected to plant some 18,000 acres to hemp in 1999, compared to 600 acres the previous year.
